rv.q: None of it is quite devastating enough, though.
Hampton’s writing is well researched, developed, sensitively and powerfully executed that we couldn’t help but be drawn into the action from the word go.
Ian McEwan’s tale of love, lust and lies loses its bite in this stage adaptation
A dizzying conveyor belt of quite leaden vignettes make up Hampton’s adaptation in a production that never manages to get into gear under the direction of Adam Penford.
Ultimately, Atonement is an often gripping drama that provides an entertaining evening while falling just short of excellence in a few key areas.
It is not his best work, but it is compelling and entertaining.
It is too much a synopsis of doomed love, not the story itself.
The result is that we never engage or care about the characters and their fate.
Atonement is an evening of tragically beautiful theatre.
